title: Research Questions & Literature Maps
description: Study form a falsifiable question, search and organize related work, establish novelty and contribution, and scope feasible experiments. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Form a falsifiable question
lessons.description: Define the dataset, metric and result that would reject the hypothesis.
lessons.conceptOverview: A research question should specify a variable, outcome and comparison that could contradict the hypothesis. Narrow questions make resource needs and success criteria clearer.
lessons.whyItMatters: A useful hypothesis can be contradicted by a specified observation.

lessons.title: Search and organize related work
lessons.description: Trace the summaries to their primary source and build a comparison matrix.
lessons.conceptOverview: Group related work by problem, assumptions and method rather than collecting titles alone. Track primary sources and distinguish reproduced findings from secondary summaries.
lessons.whyItMatters: Multiple summaries of one study are not independent evidence.

lessons.title: Establish novelty and contribution
lessons.description: Describe the specific contribution and the closest baseline.
lessons.conceptOverview: A contribution may be a method, dataset, evaluation or reproducible negative result. Compare against the closest relevant work and state the difference precisely rather than claiming broad novelty from unfamiliarity.
lessons.whyItMatters: Novelty claims require comparison with relevant prior work.

lessons.title: Scope feasible experiments
lessons.description: Choose a question the available runs can meaningfully address.
lessons.conceptOverview: Match the question to available data, compute and time. A smaller controlled study can answer a narrow question more convincingly than an underpowered attempt at a broad claim.
lessons.whyItMatters: Research scope should fit the evidence that can be collected.
